defs.def: unexpected, surprising or strange 意想不到的；令人惊奇的；奇怪的

ex.s: Marie Curie(1869-1934) was a world-famous_________and was first awarded the Nobel Prize in 1903 for her extraordinary work in radioactivity.
ex.t: 玛丽·居里（1869-1934）是一位世界著名的_________，于 1903 年因其在放射性领域的非凡工作首次获得诺贝尔奖。

ex.s: It was an extraordinary experience and something I will never forget.
ex.t: 这是一次非同寻常的经历，我永远不会忘记。

ex.s: It truly is an extraordinary “Sky Railway”.
ex.t: 这确实是一条非同寻常的“天路”。

ex.s: With each person I met, I felt a growing sense of pride as part of this extraordinary team, whose devotion to the cause shone from their eyes.
ex.t: 我每见到一个团队成员，作为这支非凡团队中的一员，我都感到越来越强烈的自豪感，他们对该事业的奉献精神从他们的眼中闪耀出来。

defs.def: not normal or ordinary; greater or better than usual 不平常的；不一般的；非凡的；卓越的

ex.s: After all, the most extraordinary stories often happen in the most ordinary places.
ex.t: 毕竟，最非凡的故事往往发生在最平凡的地方。

defs.def: arranged for a special purpose and happening in addition to what normally or regularly happens 会议等
employed for a special purpose in addition to the usual staff 紧接名词之后
